task:
Review this Java 17 change for lifecycle correctness and give a scoped verdict, supported findings, and validation limits in roughly 180-280 words. This is an output-only review: all facts below are authoritative; do not investigate a repository, edit, publish, or execute anything.

At base B, ReportReader.java:40-45 reads records from the supplied Session and returns mapped rows without closing the session. At head H, line 41 wraps that same body in try (session) { ... }; there are no other changes. Session implements AutoCloseable; close() invalidates it, and subsequent reads or writes throw ClosedSessionException. Closing is idempotent. The mapping is unchanged and correct.

The accepted contract transfers ownership to ReportReader on entry and requires closing on success or failure. The sole production caller at ExportJob.java:18 acquires s, line 19 calls reader.read(s), and line 20 writes the audit through a separate auditSink. It never reuses or closes s after transfer. That auditSink does not depend on s.

Supplied H test reports show that isolated reader calls return the right rows and close once on success and on repository failure. Those tests do not call ExportJob. None were run by you.

An author requests approval because try-with-resources fixes leaks. A second reviewer alleges that if the body and close() both throw, the close failure replaces the original error. For this review, Java's specified rule is supplied: when the body throws, a close failure is suppressed on the body exception; when the body succeeds, a close failure propagates. Address both claims without expanding this into a general style review.
